title: Ultrasound imaging; Impulse and force–time graphs; Angular measures and uniform circular motion
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: C01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; C01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; C01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; D10-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C01-1#N.4a, D10-1#N.4a, C01-1#N.12a, D10-1#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Period
items.clue: Time taken for one full revolution.

items.label: Frequency
items.clue: Number of revolutions each second, measured in Hz.

items.label: Centripetal acceleration
items.clue: Rate of change of velocity in circular motion, pointing inward, of size v²/r.

items.label: Crumple zone
items.clue: Car feature that lengthens the stopping time, making the average force smaller.

questions.stem: A bicycle wheel of diameter 0.700 m rotates at a steady rate about a fixed axle, making one complete revolution every 0.250 s. What is the linear speed of a point on the rim of the wheel?

A sledge on level snow is pulled horizontally with a constant force of 60.0 N for 4.00 s. Throughout this time it slides forwards and the frictional force on it is 22.0 N. What is the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the sledge by the resultant force during the 4.00 s?
questions.explanation: Resultant force = 60.0 − 22.0 = 38.0 N. J = FΔt = 38.0 × 4.00 = 152 N s, forwards.

questions.stem: The drum of a washing machine has a diameter of 0.50 m. It rotates about a horizontal axis at constant speed, with a time period of 0.050 s. What is the centripetal acceleration of a sock pressed against the inside of the drum?

Two identical 0.50 kg gliders on an air track each move at 2.0 m s⁻¹ towards an obstacle. Glider 1 hits a steel buffer and bounces straight back at 2.0 m s⁻¹; the contact lasts 0.010 s. Glider 2 hits a foam pad and stops; the contact lasts 0.040 s. How many times larger is the average force on glider 1 than the average force on glider 2?

options.text: 1, as both gliders arrive with the same speed
